results.term_definition: On Earth, the gravitational force is almost constant, pointing what we call downwards. But over larger distances, gravity's strength and direction vary, and those differences are called tidal forces. The Earth and the Moon, for instance, orbit a common center of mass due to their mutual gravitational attraction, but objects on the side of Earth nearer the Moon will be accelerated a bit more strongly towards the Moon, objects on the opposite side of Earth somewhat less. Earth's ocean water follows those tidal accelerations, forming "tidal bulges" directly under the Moon and on the opposite side, which produces Earth's tides.
